goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:131 & app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 — raw_html cook method returns post body completely un-sanitized, and TopicEmbed.import feeds untrusted RSS/remote content with no HTML filtering, enabling stored XSS via <script> or onerror= handlers

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new cook_method enum and changes Post#cook to return `raw` directly when `cook_method == :raw_html` (app/models/post.rb). TopicEmbed.import sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and passes `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` where `contents` comes from RSS/remote HTML (poll_feed uses `i.content` with only `CGI.unescapeHTML` and `.scrub`, and import_remote uses Readability but still produces HTML). There is no sanitization step before storing or rendering; the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore injected tags/attributes (e.g., `<script>` or `onerror=` in RSS content) can be persisted and executed, i.e., a stored XSS risk introduced by bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:4 — force: true on an already-shipped migration will silently drop and recreate the top_topics table, destroying aggregated topic stats in environments where the table exists with data

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it, which would erase any existing `top_topics` data if this migration is ever executed against a DB where `top_topics` is already present (e.g., migrate on a DB missing the schema_migrations entry, redo/reset in some workflows). This introduces a real data-loss risk compared to the previous `create_table` call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:47 — open(url).read in import_remote follows redirects without re-validating the host against embeddable_host, enabling SSRF into the private network via redirect targets

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (open-uri) on the provided URL without any post-redirect validation. Although `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` checks that the *initial* `@embed_url` host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, a URL on that host can respond with an HTTP redirect to an internal/private address, and open-uri will follow redirects by default. That would make the server fetch the redirected-to target, enabling SSRF via redirect chains while still passing the initial host check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:47 & app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — open(...) called with no open_timeout/read_timeout and no body-size limit; a slow or huge remote document can hang a Sidekiq worker indefinitely or exhaust memory

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces direct remote fetching via Ruby's open-uri without any safeguards. In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 it does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and in app/models/topic_embed.rb:47 it does `open(url).read`. Neither call supplies open_timeout/read_timeout (open-uri supports these) and `read` will load the entire response body into memory with no size cap. Since these are executed inside Sidekiq jobs (PollFeed is scheduled; RetrieveTopic triggers remote import), a slow endpoint can tie up a worker for a long time and a large response can cause excessive memory use.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 — i.content will be nil for feeds using description/summary instead of content, raising NoMethodError; with no per-item rescue and retry: false, one malformed item aborts the entire poll until the next hour
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify the same root problem: the code assumes `i.content` is present, but many feeds only provide `description`/`summary`, so `i.content` can be nil and calling methods on it (e.g., `.scrub`) will raise a NoMethodError. The candidate also adds impact details (poll aborts), but the underlying issue matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 — String#scrub was introduced in Ruby 2.1; on Ruby 2.0 this raises NoMethodError on every poll

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce `i.content.scrub` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` (line shown: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`), and it’s true that `String#scrub` is not available before Ruby 2.1. However, the diff itself does not state or constrain the supported Ruby version (no `.ruby-version`, `ruby` directive in Gemfile, etc.), so the claim that this will break “on Ruby 2.0” is not verifiable from the provided changes alone. It’s a compatibility concern, but not a confirmed defect based solely on the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:31 — $redis.setnx followed by $redis.expire is not atomic; if the process dies between the calls the key persists forever with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval for that URL; should use SET key 1 NX EX 60

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two operations are not atomic; if the process/thread dies or errors after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will remain without a TTL. Because future calls use `setnx`, retrieval for that `@embed_url` would then be blocked indefinitely. The proposed fix (atomic SET with NX and EX) directly addresses this real correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:19-35 — Check-then-create race: two concurrent imports of the same URL both see embed.blank? and both call TopicEmbed.create!, causing the second to raise RecordNotUnique and crash the job instead of falling back to the revise path

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, it first does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank enters a transaction and unconditionally calls `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)`. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, and there is no rescue around `create!`. With two concurrent imports of the same URL, both can observe `embed.blank?` before either inserts, leading the second `create!` to raise a uniqueness/RecordNotUnique exception and abort the job instead of taking the update/revise path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 — title can be nil (RSS item without title or doc.title nil from readability); combined with skip_validations: true in PostCreator, topics are created with a nil/blank title

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the `title` argument is passed straight into `PostCreator.new(user, title: title, ...)` with `skip_validations: true` and there is no guard/default if `title` is nil/blank. Callers introduced here can supply nil: Jobs::PollFeed uses `i.title` (RSS items can lack a title), and TopicEmbed.import_remote uses `opts[:title] || doc.title` where `doc.title` from readability may be nil. This makes it possible for the import path to attempt creating a topic/post with a nil/blank title, bypassing validations and/or causing a save error depending on model/DB constraints.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:12,29 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute emits public cache headers for a response whose authorization depends on request.referer, which is not part of the cache key; a shared/CDN cache can serve an authorized embed response to a non-embeddable origin

spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb — spec only stubs poll_feed and never tests actual logic: feed parsing, URL fallback to i.id, CGI.unescapeHTML/scrub handling, or TopicEmbed.import invocation; spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb lacks coverage for import_remote and absolutize_urls

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (SimpleRSS parsing, `link` vs `id` fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and calling `TopicEmbed.import`). However `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests the guard conditions in `execute` and merely asserts `poll_feed` is/ isn’t called; it never exercises `poll_feed` itself or asserts parsing/`TopicEmbed.import` behavior. Similarly, `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` covers `.import` (including `absolutize_urls` indirectly) but does not cover `.import_remote` at all, so the finding about missing coverage is accurate and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:6 — no null check on document.getElementById('discourse-comments'); if the host page omits the div, comments.appendChild throws a TypeError and the embed silently fails

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the code assigns `comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and unconditionally calls `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. If the embedding page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be null and `appendChild` will throw a TypeError at runtime, breaking the embed script. There is no null/undefined guard in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:16 — discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 is a substring match rather than strict origin equality; an origin appearing as a substring/prefix of discourseUrl would be accepted; should compare normalized origins with ===
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that using indexOf for origin validation performs a substring/prefix check rather than strict origin equality, allowing a malicious domain (e.g., one containing the trusted domain as a substring) to bypass the check. Candidate also suggests normalizing and using ===, matching the golden concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:14 — contents << "\n<hr>..." mutates the caller's string in place, surprising callers and making the sha1 depend on a side effect

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `contents << "\n<hr>..."` in `TopicEmbed.import`, which mutates the passed-in String object in place. However, in the usages introduced/modified here (RSS polling via `i.content.scrub`, readability via `doc.content`, and the disqus import path), the argument is effectively a fresh string that is not reused after the call. The SHA1 being computed after the append appears intentional (it tracks the stored post contents including the attribution/footer), not an unintended side effect. So while the mutation is technically true, the finding frames it as a clear defect; in this diff it’s not a verifiable bug/security/correctness problem impacting behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:32-34 — fallback url = i.id accepts non-HTTP Atom ids (e.g., urn:uuid:...), which TopicEmbed.import silently drops via the ^https? regex with no logging, making feed gaps hard to diagnose

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, each item’s URL is set from `i.link`, then replaced with `i.id` when the link is blank or not HTTP(S): `url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`. Atom `id` values are often non-HTTP identifiers (e.g., `urn:uuid:...`). TopicEmbed.import immediately returns unless the URL matches the same `^https?` regex, with no logging. So such feed entries will be silently skipped, creating hard-to-diagnose gaps. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:17-19 — feed_key is dead code: the 'feed-modified' key is never read or written, so the feed is fully re-imported every hour with only the sha1 revision check as protection

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` builds a Redis key (`"feed-modified:..."`) but it is never referenced anywhere else in the diff (no reads/writes, no conditional logic based on it). The job’s `poll_feed` method will therefore fetch and parse the feed and iterate all `rss.items` every hour regardless of whether the feed changed, relying only on `TopicEmbed.import`’s per-item `embed_url` lookup and `content_sha1` comparison to avoid creating/updating posts unnecessarily.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143 — Disqus import now fetches each thread's permalink live via import_remote instead of using the local XML export; dead/offline links break the import, and the --category option was removed without replacement, changing documented CLI behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff in lib/tasks/disqus.thor removes the `--category` method_option and all logic that mapped it to a `category_id`, with no new replacement parameter or behavior, so the CLI loses previously supported functionality. It also changes thread creation from a local `PostCreator` using the Disqus export data to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, which calls `open(url).read` (see TopicEmbed#import_remote) without error handling; if a thread permalink is dead/unreachable, the import can raise and abort. Both changes are directly verifiable in the diff.
